technical_and_design_decisions: Adopt Spring Boot's configuration-metadata mechanism (META-INF/spring-configuration-metadata.json) and @ConfigurationProperties for module option binding (U5).

Use Spring Boot Config Server (spring-cloud-config) as the central place for externalized configuration across XD-Admin and XD-Container, with client-side bootstrap via spring-cloud-config-client (U6).
Leverage Spring Boot Actuator's MetricRepositoryAutoConfiguration.export() API to push per-module/app metrics to a metrics backend instead of building a custom export pipeline (U4).
Refactor the job module runtime so that a child ApplicationContext is bootstrapped on job launch and closed on job completion, instead of being created at module deployment time (U2).
Use JMH (Java Microbenchmark Harness) for reproducible performance benchmarks and run them on dedicated reference hardware whose specs are published alongside the results (U1).
Migrate CI builds from current infrastructure to AWS EC2 build agents using a Jenkins EC2/spot plugin (or equivalent) with shared AMI and per-job provisioning (U8).
Diagnose the Rabbit message bus using a combination of JMX, RabbitMQ management/overview API, and async-profiler/JFR to isolate the bottleneck before applying code-level fixes (U7).
Update the existing Spring XD reference documentation (Asciidoc/Spring reference style) for the Spark module tap API and the Spark Reliable receiver semantics, including runnable examples (U3).
assumptions: A single senior Java/Spring developer (5+ years experience with Spring Framework, Spring XD, and Spring Boot) performs all work; estimates are effort, not calendar duration.
One workday equals 8 productive hours; no significant vacation, training, or meetings during the increment.
The current Spring XD codebase, build system, and CI are available and well understood at the start of the increment.
Spring XD is on Spring Boot 1.x (consistent with the actuator reference URL in U4); upgrading Spring Boot is out of scope unless forced by a user story.
AWS account with IAM permissions to create EC2 instances, security groups, AMIs, and basic networking is available (U8).
Test environments for Spark (standalone or YARN) and RabbitMQ are available for functional and performance validation (U2, U3, U7).
Estimates include development, unit tests, and developer-level integration testing; a separate QA cycle is not included.
Infrastructure-specific publishing for U1 means co-locating benchmark source, scripts, and an infrastructure.md in the spring-xd repository's benchmarks area, not building a full website.
No major refactor of Spring XD core is required beyond what is needed to deliver the user stories.
Code review is performed by the same developer acting as reviewer (lightweight self-review and pair-style review) and is folded into the relevant activities plus a small dedicated pass.
Final release engineering (artifact signing, announcement blog, staging repos) is excluded.

activities.activity_description: Review all 8 user stories, reconcile overlaps (notably U5/U6 around external configuration and U2 with the existing JobLauncher/ModuleDeployer lifecycle), produce a short design note covering Boot property source migration, lazy job context, Config Server wiring, and metrics export, and identify shared infrastructure changes needed across stories.

Author JMH-based benchmarks for the critical Spring XD paths (stream/job deployment, tap, Rabbit bus, batch job launch) and integrate them as a runnable Maven module that can be executed on a reference machine.

activities.activity_name: U1 - Document infrastructure specifics for benchmarks
activities.activity_description: Capture the exact hardware (CPU model/cores, RAM, disk, OS/JVM version), cluster topology, and JVM arguments used to run the benchmarks; publish them in an infrastructure document alongside the benchmark results so users can reproduce or compare.

activities.activity_name: U2 - Implement lazy bootstrap/shutdown of job modules
activities.activity_description: Change the job module lifecycle so that the child ApplicationContext for a job is created when the job is launched and closed when it completes (success or failure), instead of being created at module deployment. Update JobLauncher, ModuleDeployer, and any container-side runtime hooks; verify behavior for stream-created jobs and ad-hoc jobs.

activities.activity_name: U3 - Update Spark streaming tap documentation and examples
activities.activity_description: Update the Spark module reference docs to cover adding a tap at the Spark module output, including a worked example, and refresh the corresponding example modules in the spring-xd-examples repo so the documented behavior actually runs.
Add a dedicated documentation section explaining the Spark Reliable receiver (write-ahead log, at-least-once semantics, failure/recovery model, configuration knobs) with a small example.

activities.activity_name: U4 - Expose module/app metrics via Boot actuator export()
activities.activity_description: Wire each module and the admin/container apps to publish their Micrometer metrics through Spring Boot Actuator's MetricRepositoryAutoConfiguration.export() so that metrics are consumed directly from the Boot actuator API without a parallel metrics pipeline.

activities.activity_name: U5 - Migrate module options to Spring Boot property sources
activities.activity_description: Replace the XD core custom property management for module options with Spring Boot's Environment/PropertySource mechanism, bind module options via @ConfigurationProperties, and remove the duplicate option list from the runtime Control Plane.

For every built-in and example module, generate META-INF/spring-configuration-metadata.json (either via the annotation processor or hand-curated JSON) so IDEs and the Boot config metadata endpoint expose module options with their types, defaults, and descriptions.

activities.activity_name: U6 - Central external properties: server-side (Config Server)
activities.activity_description: Stand up a Spring Cloud Config Server (or equivalent git-backed config server), model the XD-Admin and XD-Container property hierarchy (application + profile + label), and publish the base property files per environment.

activities.activity_name: U6 - Central external properties: client-side (XD-Admin and XD-Container)
activities.activity_description: Integrate spring-cloud-config-client into both XD-Admin and XD-Container, wire bootstrap configuration (spring.cloud.config.*), enable fail-fast and retry as appropriate, and validate that secrets via encrypted properties work end-to-end.

activities.activity_name: U7 - Rabbit message bus: profile and isolate the bottleneck
activities.activity_description: Set up a reproducible Rabbit load test mirroring XD's stream/tap traffic, instrument the bus code and the broker via JMX and the Rabbit management plugin, collect async-profiler/JFR flame graphs, and produce a written root-cause analysis identifying the dominant bottleneck (producer/consumer, channel pooling, serialization, prefetch, broker config, etc.).

activities.activity_name: U7 - Rabbit message bus: implement performance fixes
activities.activity_description: Apply the targeted fixes identified in the profiling step (e.g., channel/confirmation pooling, batching, prefetch tuning, serializer changes, broker-side parameter changes) and re-run the same load test to confirm an improvement, capturing before/after numbers in a short report.

Define the EC2 AMI and instance type(s) for CI build agents, create the security groups, IAM role, and key material, and configure the Jenkins (or equivalent) EC2/spot plugin so that agents are spun up on demand and torn down after builds.

activities.activity_name: U8 - Migrate and validate MASTER CI builds on EC2
activities.activity_description: Port the existing MASTER-branch CI job definitions (build, test, integration, packaging) to the new EC2-based agents, run the full pipeline, fix any environment-specific breakages (paths, toolchains, network), and stabilize so builds are green and reliable.

Run an end-to-end integration pass that exercises the new lazy job bootstrap (U2), Boot-backed module options (U5), Config Server-backed admin/container config (U6), and actuator-exported metrics (U4) together on a representative cluster, and fix any regressions found.

activities.activity_name: Documentation, release notes, and operator guidance
activities.activity_description: Update the Spring XD reference documentation affected by U2/U4/U5/U6/U7 (lifecycle, metrics, configuration, Rabbit tuning), and write release notes describing the user-visible changes, migration steps, and any breaking config renames.

activities.activity_name: Final code review, polish, and merge
activities.activity_description: Perform a dedicated final pass: review all changes for consistency, remove dead code, ensure CI is green on EC2 agents (U8), and merge feature branches to MASTER.
